name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+17 district with no visible Democratic path
Incumbent Gary Palmer holds roughly a 175-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 96 percent
No public polling or expert ratings; district fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: An R+17 seat, a well-funded incumbent seeking re-election, and a challenger who has raised about $6,500 leave no apparent route to an upset; markets and district fundamentals both point to a comfortable Palmer win.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal or an unexpected incumbent stumble could put this district in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District, centered on Birmingham's southern suburbs, leans Republican by 17 points. Republican incumbent Gary Palmer is seeking another term and has raised about $1.1 million, with roughly $104,000 on hand. Democrat Maurice Mercer has raised about $6,500 and reported under $2,000 in cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets put the Republican win chance near 96 percent. The district's partisan lean, Palmer's incumbency, and the vast gap in campaign resources all point the same direction. A national environment that favors Republicans adds to the structural advantage, leaving this seat well outside the competitive battleground map this cycle.
